newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Thousands in HK walk to raise handover party funds.
newsitem.headline: Thousands in HK walk to raise handover party funds.

text.p: Thousands of people in Hong Kong took part in a charity walk on Sunday to mark the handover to Chinese rule this year and raise funds for glitzy parties planned during the historic sovereignty transfer.

The three-km (1.9 mile) "Celebration of Reunification Charity Walk", was organised by a pro-China association drawing up plans for the handover ceremonies and the Community Chest, a non-profit charity organisation.
The walk, led by Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa, raised about HK$17 million (US$2.2 million), but HK$3 million would go to the Community Chest.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, will revert to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
The handover ceremony association plans variety shows and fireworks displays during the handover.
The walk from the business district of Central to Causeway Bay's Victoria Park attracted more than 20,000 participants.
